text:
ConocoPhillips barely moved today, closing flat after a strong two-week rally of 8.5% that rode a wave of oil price strength and geopolitical tension. Oil prices jumped again—Brent crude hit $113, its highest since May—as the U.S. moved to resume strikes against Iran and pulled diplomats from Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure, raising the risk of a wider Middle East conflict that could disrupt global energy supplies.

The stock's recent gains reflect the sector's bet that these regional tensions will keep oil prices elevated and support energy company earnings. The rally also coincides with broader talk of the "energy trade" as a beneficiary of rising crude prices and supply risks, though today's flat close suggests the immediate excitement from this week's headline-making moves may be settling.
